ruleName: Actions Affecting Ball on Putting Green
title: Practice Swing Moves Ball on Putting Green
question: Your ball is on the putting green. Before making your putt, you take a practice swing and accidentally hit the ball, causing it to roll several feet away. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: Count it as your next stroke and play the ball from where it came to rest.
You receive a one-stroke penalty and must replace the ball.
There is no penalty. Replace the ball on its original spot before making your stroke.
There is no penalty. Play the ball from where it came to rest.

explanation: A practice swing is not a stroke as there was no intention to hit the ball. On the putting green, if a player accidentally causes their ball to move, there is no penalty. The ball must be replaced on its original spot before making the next stroke (Rule 13.1d(1)).

juniorVersion.title: Practice Swing Accidentally Moves Your Ball on the Green
juniorVersion.question: Your ball is sitting on the green. Before you putt, you take a practice swing, but you accidentally hit your ball and it rolls away. What should you do?

choices.text: This counts as your next shot. Play from where the ball stops.
You get one penalty stroke and put the ball back where it was.
There is no penalty. Put the ball back where it was before you hit it.
There is no penalty. Play the ball from where it rolled to.

juniorVersion.explanation: Because you didn’t mean to hit your ball with your practice swing, you don’t get a penalty. Just put your ball back in its old spot and then play your putt.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The short grass around the hole where you use your putter.
A swing you make to get ready, but not to hit the ball.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Practising by swinging next to your ball is normal, just try to be careful not to touch your ball. If it does move, remember you won’t get a penalty on the green, but you must put it back.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children might think any hit counts as a stroke, even if it’s an accident.
Some children may think you always get a penalty if the ball is moved, even on the green.
